case_title: Satya Narayana Tiwari and Anr v. State of U.P.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B; IPC s.498-A; Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 s.4
weapon: Cloth ligature around the neck; kerosene used for burning
evidence_type: Circumstantial; medical (post-mortem); recovery memos; oral testimony of father and relative
aggravating_circumstances: Victim strangulated then set on fire by at least two persons; persistent dowry demand over Maruti car with torture; false report to mislead police
high_court_outcome: Conviction under s.304-B IPC, s.498-A IPC and s.4 Dowry Prohibition Act; life for s.304-B, 3 years for s.498-A, 6 months for s.4 DPA, concurrent
offence_finally_established: Dowry death (IPC s.304-B); cruelty to wife/dowry harassment (IPC s.498-A); Dowry Prohibition Act s.4
neutral_facts: The victim, a 24-year-old woman, was married in December 1997 and died at her marital home in November 2000, about three years after the marriage. Her body was found in a lonely corner of a first-floor bedroom. Post-mortem by a panel of three doctors recorded a ligature mark about 31 x 7 cm around the neck, superficial to deep burns over the body, and a smell of kerosene. A half-burnt cloth with a knot was found around the neck. The prosecution alleged that the victim's husband and mother-in-law had demanded a car as dowry from the victim's family and persistently pressed this demand after about six months of marriage, tormenting her when it was not met. The victim's father and a relative testified that about three months before her death they visited the marital home about the demand; they were insulted and told not to return without a car. The victim had reported the mistreatment to her parents by telephone and on visits to her parental home. Recoveries from the scene included blood and a bloodstained bindi on a balcony outside the room, broken bangles inside the room, and a burnt cordless phone and burnt wire stuck to the body. The father lodged a first information report on the day of death. The mother-in-law later lodged a police report stating that the victim had committed suicide. The husband and mother-in-law absconded for several days before surrendering in November 2000, and an investigating officer testified that attempts to arrest them had failed.
physical_harm: Death by strangulation (ligature mark about 31 x 7 cm) and burning with ante-mortem burns over the body
premeditation_planning: Found: court held crime was committed with preplanning, including a false suicide report to create a defence
motive: Persistent dowry demand for a Maruti car, not met by the victim's father
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of father (PW 1) and relative (PW 2) on dowry demand and cruelty; post-mortem report; recovery memos Ex.Ka-10 and Ka-11; burnt cordless phone and wire; false report and absconding
witness_credibility: PW 1 and PW 2 found credible and corroborating; PW 1 found not to act out of malice; defence sister DW 1 found interested and not believed; defence suicide theory rejected
post_offence_conduct: Both accused absconded; attempts to arrest failed; mother-in-law lodged a false suicide report at the police station; husband surrendered 7.11.2000 and mother-in-law 13.11.2000
bail_history: Bail granted by Supreme Court on 27.10.2005; bail bonds cancelled on dismissal of appeal
trial_duration: offence: 03.11.2000; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 12.07.2005; Supreme Court: 28.10.2010
legal_representation: Appellants: Indu Malhotra, Rajesh and Vivek Jain. Respondent (State): K.T.S. Tulsi, Shail Kr. Dwivedi (AAG), R.K. Gupta and others
investigation_status: FIR lodged 03.11.2000; investigation completed; charge sheet filed; trial held
procedural_irregularity: Trial judge treated non-production of the knot as a ground against the prosecution, though the knot had been removed during post-mortem; no s.302 IPC charge was framed
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted; High Court: convicted under s.304-B, s.498-A IPC and s.4 DPA; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed, convictions upheld
defence_argument: Demand after six months did not meet the 'soon before' proximity test; no demand shown in the three months before death; death was suicide, not homicide; accused were not present and the victim's father acted with motive
legal_principle_applied: Ingredients of s.304-B IPC (Kunhiabdulla); 'soon before' tested by proximity; s.113-B Evidence Act presumption applied and not displaced; cruelty may be mental as well as physical
precedent_relied_upon: Kunhiabdulla v. State of Kerala, 2004 (4) SCC 13 (followed; distinguished on facts); Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab, AIR 1980 SC 898 (rarest of rare); Balwant v. State of Punjab, AIR 2005 SC 1504 (cited by defence, not accepted)
sentencing_rationale: Court held death sentence would be warranted for such bride burning, but could not impose it as no s.302 IPC charge was framed; High Court sentences upheld
judicial_aggravating_factors: Bride killing is barbaric; crimes against women are social crimes calling for harsh punishment; victim killed by strangulation then burning, which the court said required at least two persons
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds cancelled; accused to be taken into custody to serve remaining sentence; application for impleadment allowed
